Subject: POC: prompt set + eval dataset collection (AcmeHealth) - next steps

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC kicked off next week: 

Summary / success criteria
- Goal: Validate that Redwood Inference can reduce average latency for your chart-summarization prompts to < 400ms p50 while matching current output quality.
- Success criteria (we agreed):
  - Latency: p50 < 400ms, p95 < 900ms on representative prompt set
  - Quality: > 95% parity on key extraction fields vs. your human gold labels (sample eval)
  - Cost: projected token spend within the budget band we discussed

What we need from AcmeHealth
1) Prompt set: representative prompts (500—1,000) covering the common chart/dashboard scenarios + edge cases. CSV or JSONL is fine — include any expected system/instruction prefixes.
2) Sample logs: 2—4k anonymized examples or a stratified sample across users (redact PHI if present) — this will let us compute baseline metrics.
3) Gold labels / evaluation rubric: mapping of expected fields for at least 200 examples for initial eval.
4) Point of contact: owner for data transfer and approvals.

Proposed timeline
- Mar 4—6: data transfer + onboarding (drive link or SFTP)
- Mar 8—12: ingestion + initial eval run
- Mar 15: delivery of evaluation report and ops recommendations

Owners and roles
- AcmeHealth data owner: Alice Johnson (we'll need sign-off for sample export)
- Redwood technical lead: Aditya Rao (cc'd) — will handle ingestion and run evals
- Account lead: Ben Carter (cc'd) — commercial and timelines

Next steps
- Alice: share the prompt file and a short sample of gold labels (attach to this thread or share a Drive link).
- Marissa / Aditya: we'll confirm ingestion format and SFTP/Drive instructions and set up a Slack channel for quick ops.

I've attached a lightweight POC-eval-plan-template.xlsx you can use to map fields. If you prefer, we can take the first pass on formatting once you share a raw export.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0123

Thanks Alice — great, appreciate the fast turnaround. A few quick clarifications:

- Single-turn prompt text is fine for the initial eval (one row = one prompt). If there are multi-turn contexts you rely on, include a context_id column and we'll ingest as conversation chains.
- For gold_labels_sample.csv, column headers we usually need: prompt_id, expected_summary, key_fields.{field_name} (e.g., key_fields.diagnosis), confidence_label (optional). If easier, drop the gold labels in the template I attached and we'll map locally.

Aditya — can you pick this up for ingestion? If Alice is uploading to SFTP, we'll provide path + sample ingestion script. Ben — FYI on timeline.

Alice — we'll stand by for the SFTP upload and will confirm once we pull the files. If you prefer Drive, here's a short doc and upload link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cPOCPlan

Hi Alice / team — Aditya here (tech lead). I'll take ownership of ingestion and the initial eval run. A few technical notes and requests so we can avoid back-and-forth once the files land: 

1) Preferred formats: CSV or JSONL (newline-delimited JSON). If CSV, please ensure a header row and UTF-8 encoding.
2) Required columns for initial run: prompt_id, prompt_text, source (optional), user_segment (optional). Gold labels: prompt_id + expected_summary + any key_fields columns.
3) If you upload to SFTP, please put files under /incoming/ACME-4567/ and set permissions to allow read for "redwood_ingest". Send the SFTP path + expected filename after upload.
4) If you must redact PHI, please replace names with <REDACTED> and keep the structure intact. We'll run the eval on anonymized text.

Plan after we pull files:
- Ingest and validate schema: 1 business day
- Run baseline model and generate metrics: 2 business days
- Share preliminary report and next steps: within 5 business days of ingestion

If you want, I can run a quick schema validation against the sample CSV you attached and send back a minimal ingestion script.

Thanks — looking forward to working with you.

— Aditya Rao
